statement: You are given two strings s and goal. One shift moves the first character of s to its end; for example, "abcde" becomes "bcdea".
Return true if some number of shifts, zero or more, turns s into goal, and false otherwise.
Equivalently, goal must have the same length as s and appear as a substring of s + s.

examples.explanation: Two shifts move "ab" to the end and give "cdeab".
A shift keeps the letters in the same cyclic order, and "abced" swaps d and e, so no number of shifts produces it.

constraints: s and goal consist of lowercase English letters
